recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-5674 unless a future work-group decision changes the lower-bound rule for Timing.repeat.duration.
issue_request: FHIR-5674 asked to change the Timing duration invariant from a positive-value restriction to a non-negative-value restriction and to fix the technical constraint accordingly. Jira status is Published with resolution Persuasive.
initial_application: The issue was recorded as pre-applied. Git commit 91ec40b9322da6cf3528962f82eecaa2d6628ba5 (#5674: fix positive to non-negative) replaced the old positive wording and @value > 0 expression in source/datatypes/timing.xml with non-negative wording and @value >= 0.
additional_context: Timing remains in current core build scope: source/fhir.ini routes datatypes through datatypes.html, marks Timing normative, and defines the Timing abbreviation. Later Timing cleanup FHIR-8697 does not reverse or narrow the non-negative duration constraint. Community searches found no direct FHIR-5674 Zulip or Confluence discussion and no conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current source/datatypes/timing.xml already says duration SHALL be a non-negative value, uses duration.exists() implies duration >= 0, and has the technical expression f:duration/@value >= 0 or not(f:duration/@value). A source search found no remaining stale positive Timing duration constraint.

related_jiras.note: A later Published Timing datatype cleanup, but its resolution concerns timing.code, offsets, examples, and notes rather than the FHIR-5674 non-negative duration constraint.
